checks.topic: compressed source image versus arbitrary photon L2
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: H_emit is the finite span of orthonormal V_lambda|Ji M> including final spin. It is a source-coupled image with fixed energy/radial mode, not arbitrary photon L2 or every independent angular harmonic. Sampling is bounded on its canonical finite harmonic representatives only.

checks.topic: all integer ranks, parity and L0
locators: printed320/PDF15 Eq3.41 notes(i)–(ii) and parity discussion
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: For fixed compatible good spins and definite parities, every allowed integer photon rank has one E/M type. Complete triangle coupling includes L0 only where possible, but projection -q=+/-1 makes its CG zero; dropping it preserves the closure. The discussed photon space is nonempty.

locators: RB67 printed316/PDF11 Eq3.24 and WE premise
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: At theta0 m=q and a sampled final M_f fixes initial M=M_f+q, giving no cross-M blocks. The squared 3j recoupling and product-state completeness give weighted CG sum 2Ji+1 for each valid q. Trace Q_M=(2Ji+1)n_valid_q/2; phases q^pi do not change this norm.

checks.topic: three sharp spectra and source witnesses
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: Independent B/Q and two-row spectra reproduce kappa2,5,7. A has one valid-helicity peak block; B/C peak at M0 with parallel helicity rows. All recorded source amplitude witnesses are normalized eigenvectors and reach W=kappa. Sharpness is on complete H_emit, not every fixed preparation or real nucleus.

CG coupling intertwines each emitted image with spin Ji. H_emit is rotation invariant and output helicity-gauge/final-spin factors are unitary, so E_Rn=U_emit E_n U_emit_dagger. Independent positive theta pi/3 factorial sampling exactly matches saved Etheta, U and covariance. The all-direction theorem is representation-based, not inferred from one check.

For any helicity effect 0<=P<=I, E_P=B_dagger(P tensor I_final)B is between0 and E_unpol. Source x/y Gram effects match and sum to E_unpol. This controls positive partial intensities; signed Stokes differences or normalized ratios require their own width/denominator argument.

Normalized state differences have trace0. E_density/kappa is an effect, so trace-distance variational characterization gives |Tr E Delta|<=kappa D. Equivalently center E by(kappa/2)I before the Holder bound. Unnormalized rate/state differences do not share this premise.

checks.topic: W average1 versus density per steradian
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: Integrated Gram gives integral E dOmega/(4pi)=I. W is dimensionless with angular average1, while probability density per steradian is W/(4pi); its error constant is kappa/(4pi). Polar intensities share the W convention and sum to W.

checks.topic: distance space and partial trace restriction
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: The compression norm is in common H_emit including final spin. D must be taken there or after retaining a common purifier. A smaller photon-only D cannot be substituted without a new point-operator/support compression audit in that output space.

checks.topic: retained normalization and changed initial density
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: Same initial rho with S>0 and S_R>0 permits old95 D<=sqrt(e). At e0 use V=V_R directly; e1 has no normalized retained reference. A changed fitted rho adds D_initial and caps the sum at1. e is a total omitted photon-rate fraction, not qR or a pair ratio.

The same independently calibrated nonnegative kernel, with integral1 in the stated angular measure, forms a convex mixture of0<=E_n<=kappa I and retains the bound. A model-dependent acceptance renormalization is postselection rather than this fixed mixture.

CPTP decreases distance but may leave H_emit, change angular support or modes. An output point-density norm or pullback requires its own audit. The old95 bounded-bin effect bound remains valid separately. Signed/ill-conditioned unfolding and noisy efficiency correction are not controlled by this theorem.

checks.topic: old nodes, conditional ratios and unknown spins
checks.grounding_and_retained_boundary: A finite absolute kappa does not establish a retained density or success floor. The old node and rare-postselection counterexamples remain. Constants depend on fixed spin/subspace; a finite independent candidate set can take its audited maximum, while unbounded unknown spins cannot use2/5/7 universally.

RB provides coherent amplitude/phase/normalization/triangle premises. The finite-space closure, spectra, kappa and density-error theorem are task derivations. supported_relations.closure: sum_allowed_L(2L+1)|CG|^2=2Ji+1 for each valid helicity; L0 contributes zero at projection +/-1.
supported_relations.trace_bound: Tr Q_M=(2Ji+1)n_valid_q/2; norm E_density=max_M norm Q_M<=max_M TrQ_M.
supported_relations.case_kappa: 2 for3/2->1/2,5 for2->2,7 for3->1 with the specified parity-mode spaces.
supported_relations.uniform_absolute_bound: |Delta W(n)|<=kappa D_full<=kappa sqrt(e) under common normalized initial-state truncation assumptions.
supported_relations.polar_intensity: 0<=E_P(n)<=E_unpol(n)<=kappa I for a positive bounded helicity analyzer.

required_reuse_boundaries: Fix compatible Ji/Jf, definite parities, one E/M type for every allowed integer rank, nonempty photon space and common energy/radial mode. L0 is not a photon mode.
Point evaluation is bounded only after compression to the specified finite source-emitted image; arbitrary photon L2 remains outside.
Sharp constants are operator norms on complete H_emit and have ideal source witnesses. They do not guarantee saturation for every fixed preparation or microscopic nuclear realization.
Use D in the common emitted space including final spin, or retain a common purifier. Do not substitute an unaudited smaller photon-only D with the same kappa.
kappa D requires positive E/kappa<=I and normalized trace-zero state difference. W has angular average1; per-steradian density divides the bound by4pi.
Positive partial polarization intensities inherit kappa. Signed Stokes differences and normalized polarization ratios are separate observables and need their spectral-width or denominator controls.
The old sqrt(e) replacement needs the same initial rho and positive S_R; a changed rho adds D_initial. Zero/complete-omission endpoints need the old explicit handling.
A common nonnegative angular kernel normalized to integral1 in the same measure gives a convex average and retains kappa. Model-dependent acceptance renormalization does not fit that argument.

A generic CPTP channel may leave H_emit. Output point operators or pullbacks need new support/norm audits even though state distance contracts. Signed inverse/unfolding and statistical errors are not supplied by this bound.
Old relative-density nodes and rare conditional-filter counterexamples remain; absolute error creates no nonzero probability floor.

Unknown/unbounded spin candidates do not share the constants2,5,7. Ideal spectral witnesses do not establish physical prior, nuclear realization, actual detector performance or finite-count significance.
